To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the set of uniformly perfect public equilibiria for a public monitoring repeated game is robust to nearby private monitoring repeated games if and only if every player is informationaly small in the sense of being able to be replaced by another player who has the same payoff structure and who can be replaced by yet another player who has a payoff structure close to his, and so on.

(i) the set of uniformly perfect public equilibriain a repeated game with perfect monitoring is robust to private monitoring when every player is informationaly small and (ii) this result can be extended to the case of uniformly strict perfect equilibria.

(1) the robustness result holds for any public coordination device and any private signal distribution, (2) the robustness is uniform over all nearby private monitoring games, (3) the set of robust equilibria is the same as the set of strict perfect public equilbria, (4) a necessary and sufficient condition for the result is that every player is small, and (5) the result holds even when players have private discount factors that differ by a factor of 2.
